rationale: Across the available literature describing Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome (STISS; OMIM #617516) caused by monoallelic PSMD12 variants, limb manifestations are consistently documented as distal, preaxial, or minor digital anomalies (including brachydactyly, polydactyly, camptodactyly, syndactyly, and minor skeletal anomalies such as ectopic fingernails). No individual with STISS has been reported with severe terminal transverse or longitudinal limb reduction malformations (such as phocomelia, ectrodactyly, or severe oligodactyly seen in Cornelia de Lange or Holt-Oram syndrome cohorts), making the presence of severe terminal limb absence an effective exclusion criterion.

evidence.text: PSMD12 alterations in Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome are characterized by distal digital anomalies such as brachydactyly, polydactyly, or camptodactyly, without severe longitudinal or transverse terminal reduction defects.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact penetrance of specific digital anomalies (e.g. preaxial polydactyly vs. brachydactyly vs. syndactyly) across all published PSMD12 variants stratified by variant type (missense vs. nonsense/frameshift)?
new_directions.rationale: Determining precise variant-specific digital anomaly penetrance will confirm if specific PSMD12 protein domains drive particular limb and skeletal findings.

new_directions.question_text: Do mouse or zebrafish models of psmd12 haploinsufficiency display altered sonic hedgehog (SHH) or anterior-posterior limb bud patterning to mechanistically explain the restriction to preaxial digital anomalies?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying how proteasome subunit insufficiency alters developmental signaling pathways in the limb bud would explain why preaxial digital phenotypes occur while major longitudinal axes remain preserved.
